title: Edit Video by Typing
subtitle: How AI turns chat prompts into cuts, clones, and transitions
intro: Your video editor just got a tombstone: RIP Video Editing 1985-2025. Now you edit by chatting, not dragging clips.
takeaway: Prompt-based editing trades hands-on control for speed, so use words for rough cuts and hands for final polish.

sections.heading: Analogy: your talking assistant editor
sections.body:
Imagine you hire an assistant who edits video for you. You say 'remove silences, add smooth cuts, make an avatar say this line' and they do it. You don't drag clips on a timeline anymore; you give instructions in plain text.

That's prompt-based editing. But why would you trust words instead of your hands?

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: speed you don't pay for twice
sections.body:
Manual editing in DaVinci, iMovie or CapCut takes hours of cutting and syncing. AI tools like HeyGen turn text into video with a cloned avatar — one creator got 50M+ views with 'AI René'.

Transcript-based editing lets you delete a word and the video cut follows. Veo 3 even lets you use JSON prompts for precise lighting and invisible cuts. That speed is powerful, but speed hides a cost.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when words guess wrong
sections.body:
AI guesses what 'make it cinematic' means, and two prompts can give two different styles for the same idea. Avatar clones can look fake, auto-cuts can remove the wrong pause, and JSON control only helps if you know what to specify.

If you rely only on chat commands, you lose fine control. So learn when to type and when to tweak by hand.

quiz.q: What does transcript-based editing let you do?
options: Delete a word in text to cut the video
quiz.why: Your saves show transcript editing links text deletions directly to video cuts.

quiz.q: Why use a JSON prompt in Veo 3 instead of a normal prompt?
options: It gives precise control over lighting, style and cuts
It is required for all videos
quiz.why: The Veo 3 save compares normal vs JSON prompts and shows JSON gives more precise cinematic control.

quiz.q: What breaks or goes wrong if you rely only on chat commands?
options: AI always picks the exact style you wanted
You lose fine control — clones look fake and auto-cuts remove wrong pauses
quiz.why: AI guesses meaning, so same idea can render in different styles and auto-edits can cut the wrong moment.

extra: HeyGen example of 50M+ views shows avatar cloning at scale, but likeness rights and disclosure matter.
